sanskrit_verse: सवर्णेभ्यः सवर्णासु जायन्ते हि सजातयः / अनिन्द्येषु विवाहेषु पुत्राः संतानवर्धनाः // यज्ञवाल्क्यस्मृतिः १.९०
transliteration: savarṇebhyaḥ savarṇāsu jāyante hi sajātayaḥ / anindyeṣu vivāheṣu putrāḥ saṃtānavardhanāḥ // YajñS_1.90
sph_interpretive_translation: From unions between persons of the same varṇa, children of pure lineage are born; in marriages free from blame, sons conducive to the continuation of the family line arise.
jurisprudential_principles: Authority originates from dharmic alignment of birth and union
Causation flows through conscious selection and spiritual compatibility
Capacity-based responsibility arises from continuity of ancestral dharma
Restoration logic resides in preservation of generational integrity
Consciousness alignment manifests through adherence to svadharma
executable_legal_axioms: IF union occurs within same varṇa THEN offspring inherit full familial rights
IF marriage aligns with śāstric guidelines THEN lineage continuity is preserved
IF no violation of dharma in procreation THEN child holds full inheritance eligibility
IF parental union lacks social or dharmic censure THEN progeny entitled to ancestral duties
supreme_court_application: In adjudication concerning lineage, legitimacy, or succession, courts must first assess whether the marital union adheres to dharmic norms ensuring continuity of varṇic order. Only those unions unmarked by transgression qualify for automatic recognition of filial and property rights.
nyaya_and_non_punitive_alignment: Pramāṇa establishes that purity of lineage results from conformity to svadharma. Anupūrvaśaḥ indicates that disruption in lineage leads to imbalance in societal harmony. Thus, restoration lies in reaffirming correct unions rather than punishing deviations.
restorative_enforcement_protocols: Guided re-alignment of familial consciousness toward svadharma
Re-establishment of ancestral connection through ritual purification
Integration of lineage disruption through conscious rectification
final_declaration: By the Supreme Pontiff of Hinduism, Bhagavan Nithyananda Paramashivam, this law stands established: lineage flows from dharmic union, and its continuity is secured through conscious adherence to svadharma. There is no punishment—only restoration. Dharma prevails.
